newsitem.title: CHINA: China changes site of nuclear power plant.
newsitem.headline: China changes site of nuclear power plant.

text.p: A Chinese nuclear official said on Monday that authorities have decided to move the site of a proposed nuclear power plant to eastern China from the northeast to meet a greater thirst for energy in that region.

The multi-billion dollar nuclear plant was originally slated for Wafangdian city in Liaoning province but authorities changed the site to Lianyungang in Jiangsu province, the official with the China National Nuclear Corp said.
The official denied a Sunday report in Hong Kong's South China Morning Post that the project had been moved because the Liaoning provincial government was unable to raise its share of the funds.
The change was made to meet a greater demand for energy in fast-growing Jiangsu province, he said.
"It has nothing to do with Liaoning's economic situation," the official said. He declined to provide further details.
Under the original plan, construction on the first phase of the plant was due to begin in 1998 and would involve putting two 1,000-megawatt pressurised water reactors into service by 2004.

The first phase was estimated to cost $4 billion. Moscow had offered Beijing a 15-year, $2 billion low-interest loan. The Liaoning government, China National Nuclear Corp and the Northeast Electric Group were to raise the other $2 billion.
Beijing has increasingly looked to nuclear power as an answer to the country's growing thirst for energy.
